## Verdict

**The key is not sound.** Its two headline verdicts (q9 = 5.015336 GHz, q10 = 5.448253 GHz) are correct and its tolerances are well chosen, but a large fraction of the *reasoning* — including the two mechanisms it names as the session's transferable lessons — is wrong on the archive's own numbers. One of the six "unresolved" verdicts (q6) is contradicted by a line sitting in plain view in the run the key itself nominates as decisive, and a second (q4) is rejected for a physically impossible reason. Below, everything is re-derived from `D:\work\dataset\SNU_1Q\2026-08-02\` (`ds_raw.h5`, `data.json`, `node.json`, `quam_state/state.json`) and the 08-03 session.

---

## A. The "band-edge artifact" section is a misdiagnosis, and it propagates

This is the most serious defect, because the key uses it as a *control* to disqualify two other qubits.

The key writes: *"q10's obviously spurious spike at 6.4442 in run 67 (IF +504, alongside its real 5.4482 peak) … Run 67's q10 panel is the control: a real peak and a Nyquist-edge spike side by side in one trace."*

Re-derived (q10 LO = 5.940 GHz, MW-FEM sampling rate 1.0 GS/s, both read from `quam_state`):

| feature | key's label | measured | mechanism | implied true f | q10 truth at that flux |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| run 67 upper spike | 6.4442 | **6.448150** (IF +508.15) | own Nyquist image (LO + IF − 1 GHz) | 5.448150 | 5.448253 → **Δ 0.10 MHz** |
| run 67 lower spike | "real peak 5.7767" | 5.776650 (δ = −280.75) | co-played q9 tone (q9 centre 5.729 + δ) | 5.448250 | 5.448253 → **Δ 0.003 MHz** |
| run 68 "Nyquist spike" | 5.87664 | 5.876650 (δ = +419.25) | co-played q9 tone (q9 centre 5.029 + δ) | 5.448250 | 5.448253 → **Δ 0.003 MHz** |

All three "spurious" features are **q10's own 0→1 transition**, reached by multiplexed cross-drive (q9's simultaneously played saturation tone landing on q10) and, in one case, by the DAC's Nyquist image. They agree with the verified 5.448253 GHz to 3 kHz, 3 kHz and 0.10 MHz. Two of the three are not Nyquist effects at all: run 68's 5.87665 is IF **+476.65 MHz**, *below* the 500 MHz Nyquist limit.

Consequences:

1. **Wrong run.** 6.4442 is run **64**'s q10 fit (`6444201000`), not run 67's; run 67's fit is 5.776688 and its second spike is at 6.4482. The key attributes run 64's number to run 67.
2. **Self-contradiction.** The session note says the run-67 spike sits *"alongside its real 5.4482 peak"*; the q10 entry says run 67 *"cannot contain 5.4482 at all."* The latter is correct — run 67's q10 span is 5.5574–6.5572 GHz. The former is false.
3. **The "real peak at 5.7767" has no owner.** At run 67 q10 sits at joint_offset −0.114, where its frequency is 5.448253. 5.7767 is neither its fundamental nor any rung (rungs go *down*). Calling it "real" and 6.448 "spurious" is arbitrary; the figure shows two spikes of essentially equal height (0.25 vs 0.24 mV) and equal width (FWHM 3.0 MHz both).
4. **The IF window is stated wrongly.** "+480 to +520 MHz … at or past the MW-FEM's 1 GS/s Nyquist edge" — +481 (q4) and +495 (q17) are *below* 500 MHz and are not aliased at all. Only +508/+517 alias. And 6.605 − 6.088 = **+517 MHz**, not the "+520" claimed.

## B. q4: rejected for a reason that does not exist, on evidence stronger than stated

The key declines to name 6.4675 GHz because it "sits at a drive IF of +481 MHz … the same IF window … demonstrated to be an artifact twice in this session," and because it "fails to appear at the lowest powers."

* +481 MHz IF **cannot alias** (Nyquist = 500 MHz at 1 GS/s). The requested tone is produced, merely rolled off outside the ±400 MHz spec band.
* The "demonstration" is section A, which is a misdiagnosis.
* The evidence is understated. The key says "Two runs at one flux point." Three runs at joint_offset +0.050572 agree:

| run | mux? | feature | powers | |z| |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 22 | yes | 6.4662 | −27.8 … −11.5 dBm | 3–13 |
| 29 | yes | 6.4669 | −29.1 … −10.9 dBm | 5–12 |
| 30 | **no** | 6.4677 | −27.2 … −10.4 dBm | 11–**29** |

  Reproduced to <1 MHz, and *strongest in the non-multiplexed run* — so it is not crosstalk.
* Run 30 shows not two features but a five-rung ladder: **6.4677 / 6.3826 / 6.2926 / 6.1974 / 6.0964**, gaps 85.1 / 90.0 / 95.2 / 101.0 MHz, each appearing at successively higher power. That is the family's own signature. The node's 6.19–6.24 answers land on rung 4.
* "Fails to appear at the lowest powers" is fair as far as it goes (nothing at −41.6…−29.6), but it is the *first* line to appear, which is the rule the key itself quotes.

"Unresolved" may still be the defensible call absent a 1-D, but every stated reason for it is wrong.

## D. Two other "not real / probably real" calls use inconsistent standards

**q17's bright 6.583/6.605 line.** The key says it is a Nyquist artifact whose *"apparent flux dependence is weak and inconsistent across runs at identical flux."* Both halves are wrong:

* At identical flux (+0.100294) runs 22 and 29 give **6.6058 both**, and run 30 gives the same 6.598–6.606 depression. It is perfectly consistent at identical flux.
* Matched power (+4 dBm) and matched flux, mux vs non-mux: run 22 **z −58**, run 29 **z +35**, run 30 (non-mux) **z −4**. It is a *multiplexing* artifact, not a band-edge one — and the sign flips between two runs at the same flux and power, which no spectroscopic line does. (q11's crosstalk, which the key does diagnose correctly, gives z +27 / +22 / **+3** on the same test.) Right conclusion, wrong mechanism — and the wrong mechanism is what is then used against q4.

**q15's 5.6115.** The key calls it *"probably a real transition of this qubit rather than an instrument artifact"* because it *"MOVES WITH FLUX in the right direction and by a plausible amount."* But (i) q15's `phi0_voltage` is **0.0** — its flux axis is uncalibrated and there is no frequency-vs-flux arch for it anywhere in the session, so "the right direction" is not assessable; (ii) it appears only in multiplexed runs, and only above +4.9 dBm — the ceiling of run 30, the one non-mux control — so the crosstalk test the key applied to q11 was never run here. At matched powers ≤ +4.9 dBm, mux and non-mux are indistinguishable (|z| ≤ 8.7 everywhere). The same evidence that condemns q11 is treated as exculpatory for q15.

*"the vs_power maps for q9 at 10-20 shots (runs 30, 45, 61, 69) are essentially featureless once the background is removed — none of them could have produced this answer."*

Run 30's q9 map is not featureless. It contains a four-rung ladder — **5.7822 (z 5→14) / 5.6994 (z 2→14) / 5.6101 / 5.5145** — *and*, at the two coldest useful powers (−41.6 to −29.6 dBm), an elevated stationary feature at **5.8583–5.8646 GHz, z +8 to +10**, which fades as power rises while the 5.7822 rung grows. That is the answer (5.862671), visible in the map, behaving exactly as the family manual says the fundamental should. So run 30 *could* have produced it — and, read carelessly, could equally have produced 5.7822. Both halves of the key's statement fail, and the failure mode it hides (a four-rung ladder with a weak top rung) is the most instructive thing in q9's data.
